note: Survival mode's numbers (spec section 7). Built so far: `map`, the path map of a stage (rules 1.40; spec rules 7 to 12; build step 2); the run's start, the encounter generator, the fights' rewards and the node panels (rules 1.41; spec rules 2, 5, 13 to 24, 26; build step 3). The other keys of section 7 are added by the later build steps. Every number is provisional.

run.about: Rules 1.41 (spec rules 2, 5, 10): the credits each character starts a run with (rules 1.52: 0; the loadout's unspent budget is the starting purse; it was 150), the HP a character dead in a won fight comes back at, the first stage's setting.

loadout.about: Rules 1.52 (Leon, 14 Nov 2026: 'Survival will give you one low level melee, one low level gun, a bow, one of the 4 focus and a budget'; corrected the same day: 'only one weapon'). The camp before node 1: each character takes ONE free weapon: the most basic of a weapon archetype (`archetypes`), ONE free focus from `focuses` (either may be declined; declining gives nothing back), and spends `budget` credits on the shop's menu (`counter`, `stock`) at shop prices (credits.ts priceOf, the one price door). What is not spent is the character's starting purse. A gun comes with `gun.loaded` magazine loaded and `gun.spare` spare (a gun loaded round by round: that many magazines' worth of loose rounds); a bow with its quiver full (its own magazine in weapons.json). A core-fuelled focus comes with `focus_with`. Everything else is bought from the shop's own menu (`counter`, `stock`).

archetypes.about: Leon, 14 Nov 2026 (binding): "freelist get the most basic one of all the weapon achetype, then we put the same weapon type but better in the rack shop, and identical weapon too, so you can dualwield or upgrade your choice". An archetype is a weapons.json family as the data groups it (`family` its mastery_family, `category` its category; `skip` ids that are not gear one carries). Its free weapon is its cheapest weapon by priceOf (Standard grade); the rack holds that weapon again (a second to carry or dual-wield) and the next weapon up by price in the archetype (one step). Computed by the engine (run/loadout.ts archetypeWeapons), checked by tools/validate.py. Families left out are in `left_out`.

left_out.heavy: launchers, flamers and belt-fed or rotary guns: support weapons, not a first weapon (a call for Leon)
left_out.mana_arms: the focus weapons (the Evoker blade, the Emanator katana and gauntlet, the core rifle...): each is a focus and a weapon at a focus-weapon's price (a call for Leon)
left_out.thrown: grenades and charges: on the Thrown shelf at the shop's price

counter.about: The paid shelves are the shop's own menu (Leon, 14 Nov 2026: '1 weapon for free, take anything else with cost from the shop menu'): every shelf of `shop.always` but the restock (run/shop.ts counterLines, its prices, its keys), then `stock`.

stock.about: The camp's gear shelf beside the weapon rack: a second focus, body armour (`armour:<class>`, rules.json armor.classes prices) and worn pieces, standard grade, a FIXED list (every player sees the same choices). The weapons are the rack's, by archetype (`archetypes`).

recommended.about: The Recommended button (and the host's Start for an away player): the focus of the character's door skill with the most points (none without one); the free weapon of the first `weapon` row's archetype that fits (a caster with a focus takes the pistol, one-handed, so the focus sits in the off hand; Raw Power above Dexterity a heavy blade; else the rifle); then its profile's `buys` in order while the budget pays (profile: the focus's fuel, core or mp; else gun or melee by the weapon), then the weapon's ammunition while it pays.

stage.about: Rules 1.41 (spec rule 19, sections 5.4 and 11.1): what a stage multiplies. Stage s: the bulk target x (1 + bulk x (s - 1)), the pressure cap x (1 + pressure x (s - 1)), credits x (1 + credits x (s - 1)), XP x xp[s - 1] (the last repeats); Elites and Bosses stand min((s - 1) x elite_up.per, elite_up.max) levels above the fight level. Step 3 plays stage 1, where every term is 1.

rounds.about: Rules 1.41 (spec rule 17): the target rounds R of a fight by node kind; a plain fight at depth early_depth or less is fight_early.

tiers.about: Rules 1.41 (spec rule 16, section 5.1): each tier's bulk (rifle-turns to remove it over a Soldier's) and pressure (Soldier-turns it deals a round) at equal level, in Soldier-equivalents (SE).

share.about: Rules 1.41 (spec rule 20): an Elite or a Boss spawns scaled by the party's size N (index N - 1): its HP and its damage; it costs its bulk x hp and its pressure x damage.

map_size.about: Rules 1.41 (spec rule 22): the fight's map by its units (the party and the foes): up to `units`, a square of `size` tiles, generated (rules 1.45, `layout`) or cropped from the middle of the open ground; the squad starts in the columns `squad_cols` (the west edge).

layout.about: Rules 1.45 (spec rule 22, section 4.3): the fight's map, generated from the node's own stream. `use`: `generated`, or `open_ground` for step 3's crop (the switch; also the fallback when no try passes). Stamps (`stamp_count` by map size) from the setting's list, turned and mirrored, `stamp_gap` apart past a ring of one kept tile, never in a start zone (the squad's first `zone_cols` columns; the enemy line and `foe_zone` columns either side); loose cover (one in `full_every` full; half cover in straight runs of `cover_run` tiles) near every start (`start_cover_reach`), until every tile outside the zones is within `cover_reach` of cover, and up to `cover_share`'s floor; `barrels` beside cover; the setting's props; `difficult` patches; a hazard patch (`hazard_size`) only where the template allows one (its `hazard`) and by the setting's chance; `dressing` tiles for the renderer. A try that fails the checks drops a stamp; after `tries`, the open ground. `grounds` and `dress_pieces`: how many of each a kit holds. `legend`: the characters the stamps use beyond the maps legend (`d` an open door).

room.name: A small room with two ways in

alley_wall.name: An alley wall with a door

xp.about: Rules 1.41 (spec section 3.1): f(d) = base + per_depth x (d - 1) to each character; an Elite x elite, the Boss x boss, a cache x cache; rules 1.48: the vault's guard x vault_guard, its chest x vault.

credits.about: Rules 1.41 (spec section 3.1): c(d) = base + per_depth x d to each character; an Elite x elite, the Boss x boss, a cache x cache; rules 1.48: the vault's guard x vault_guard, its chest x vault.

ammo_pack.about: Rules 1.41, 1.51 (spec rules 23, 52): the supply pack. After a won fight (or at a cache or the vault) each character gets, with n this many by the node: n magazines' worth of rounds for every gun it carries (x the stat run_ammo); with a focus of a kind in `core_doors` carried, after a fight the spare cores it burnt in it back (none burnt, none back), at most `cores_max` x n, and at a cache or the vault `cores` x n; with a focus of a kind in `mp_doors` carried, `mp_share` x n of its max MP (cores and MP x the stat run_supply).

rewards.about: Rules 1.41 (spec rule 26): the weapon pick of `offer` weapons after a won fight, the first for the character's own door or weapon category; rarity by node kind, capped by `ceiling` (by stage, the last repeats); price at most base + per_depth x d + per_stage x (s - 1), x elite or boss; or credits instead, instead_rate of the cheapest offer's price.

nodes.about: Rules 1.41, 1.42, 1.43: what each kind of node without a fight says on its panel, to the player (docs/design/ui-screens.md, Writing for the player); the shop opens full screen (rules 1.42).
nodes.shop: A shop. Buy ammunition and gear, sell what you don't need, repair and upgrade.
nodes.forge: The armourer's Forge. Upgrade and repair a weapon, buy mods and armour pieces, get fitted for heavier armour.
nodes.training: The drill yard. Each of you trains once for free, and once more for credits.
nodes.shrine: A shrine. Each of you takes one thing: a rite, a piece of its patron's lore, or a token.
nodes.event: A crossroads. A broker has trades on the table. Take one each, or walk on.
nodes.cache: A cache. Credits, ammunition, a little experience and a pick of kit.
nodes.rest: A safe place. Everyone heals in full and a new session begins. Each of you may train once before moving on.
nodes.vault: The vault, its guard down. Each of you takes credits and a pick of three weapons better than anything sold this stage. Then back to the trail.

tips.about: Rules 1.41 (spec 8.2): the path map's hover card for each kind of node, to the player: what you do there and what you get; the engine adds the XP and credits it pays.
tips.fight: A fight. Win for XP, credits, ammunition and a pick of three weapons.
tips.elite: A hard fight: an Elite and its line. Better pay and a better pick.
tips.gate: The Gate. Every trail passes it: an Elite and its line. Better pay and a better pick.
tips.boss: The stage's Boss. The best pay and pick of the stage. Win to clear the stage.
tips.shop: A shop. Ammunition, cores, supplies and the day's gear. Sell, repair and upgrade.
tips.forge: A Forge. Upgrades and repairs, mods, armour pieces and armour fitting.
tips.training: A drill yard. One training each for free, a second for credits.
tips.shrine: A shrine. A rite, a piece of lore or a token from its patron.
tips.rest: A rest. Everyone heals in full, and each of you may train once.
tips.cache: A cache. Credits, ammunition, a little XP and a pick of kit. No fight.
tips.event: A crossroads. A broker offers trades: take one, or walk on.
tips.vault_guard: A guarded vault, off the trail. A fight harder than an Elite's. Win it to open the vault, then come back to this trail. You may pass it by.
tips.vault: The vault. Credits and a pick of three weapons a grade above this stage's. No fight.

grade_up.about: Rules 1.43 (spec rules 37, 38, 43; section 11.2): the grade step of one carried weapon or focus. At a place of `places` (a shop, a Forge) to Fine or Masterwork at `price` of the grade it reaches x the place's factor; the Relic step only at a Forge, at its own price (no factor), from stage relic_from_stage; per_visit steps a character a visit; an armourer's chit (`chit`, items.json) pays one Fine or Masterwork step in place of the credits. cut_rate: the Crossroads' off-books step (a share of the shop's price).

repair.about: Rules 1.50: the repair service of a shop and a Forge (run/repair), the Core Rules' gunsmith (Weapons v2, Durability rule 4: 100% restored for `rate` of the weapon's price) priced by the share missing: max(`floor`, rate x priceOf(the item at its grade, no mods) x (missing / full)) x the place's factor, rounded up to whole credits. Any carried weapon or shield with wear (a hand or the pack) comes back to full; a focus and armour do not wear. No limit a visit.

forge.about: Rules 1.43 (spec rule 44): the Forge's rolled stock, `slots` mods and worn pieces made for what its visitors carry (a mod for a slot one of them has free, a worn piece better than one of them wears), each at its price; the grade step's factor is grade_up.places.forge.

armour_fit.about: Rules 1.43 (spec rule 44): the Forge fits the next armour class for its price, until body armour becomes items (Equipment 2.0). Rules 1.52: Class 1 added (100), now that a Survival character may set out with no body armour. The class's own gate (Pain Threshold, a trait's cap) holds.

boon_cap.about: Rules 1.43 (spec rule 31): the run power a character may carry, in percent of a rifle-turn: its boons, a shrine's token, the graft and the named property of every Relic it carries add their `worth` against `cap`.

boon_pick.about: Rules 1.44 (spec rules 30, 31): after each Boss every character picks one boon of `offer`, rolled from the tile's pool (`pools`), then from every pool when the tile's runs short; a boon held, or one whose worth would pass the run's cap, is not offered: a utility boon (worth 0) takes its place.

world.about: Rules 1.44 (spec rule 32): after the boon, `offer` tiles (at least `min`) are offered for the next stage, each a setting not yet played this run where possible, and only a setting that is ready (its Boss, its kinds and a boon pool in data).

graft.about: Rules 1.43 (spec rule 42, the back-room graft): the graft is a relic made of a boon of the tile's pool and a cut to max HP for the run (`hp_mult`, the stat `hp`); its worth is the boon's.

train.about: Rules 1.43 (spec rule 39): the rest's small training, one a character: drill on a weapon it carries (addDrill), study (addStudy, a Sigil user), practice (addPractice, an Outburst user), or Devotion XP (shiftDevotion, the Faithful).

training.about: Rules 1.43 (spec rule 45): the training ground's big training, one a character for free and a second (the most is `most`) for extra_price credits: drill, study or practice (Devotion is the shrine's).

shrine.about: Rules 1.43 (spec rule 46): one offer a character: the rite (Devotion XP by patrons.json gain.rite_kept), a knowledge piece for an Atheist (grantPiece), or the patron's token, a boon of the tile's pool of worth at most token_max_worth, at most tokens_per_stage a character a stage, on the cap.

lasting.about: Rules 1.43 (spec rules 41, 43): an Elite's and a cache's armour-or-item pick of `offer`, at least `min` of them lasting (a mod for a slot the main weapon has free, a worn piece better than the one worn there; never two consumables); the rest from `fill`. The gate's pick holds an armourer's chit in stage chit_gate; an Elite from stage chit_from_stage may roll one, one chance in chit_odds.

trades.about: Rules 1.43 (spec rule 42): a Crossroads offers `offer` of these trades, each a cost and a gain the engine takes and gives (`do` names which); each character takes at most one, or walks on. The wayside shrine is free and once a stage.

vault.about: Rules 1.48 (Leon, 13 Nov): the one dead end of a map. Its guard's fight has an Elite fight's budget x guard_factor (bulk and pressure; the template vault_watch, the setting's named vault_guard); its chest gives each character credits (`credits.vault` x c(d)) and a pick of three weapons or foci at grade_up grades above the stage's pick ceiling, at most grade_max (stage 1 Masterwork, from stage 2 Relic), or credits instead.

shop.about: Rules 1.42 (spec rules 25 to 27, section 8.3): the shop. `always`: the counter, never sold out, at the fixed price of credits.ts priceOf, in shelves (`guns`: a magazine or the rounds of every gun the party carries, worked out per visit; `restock`: the persistent class resources, a point at a time; the others list ids); `per`: how many one purchase gives (a stack of rounds). `stock`: the rolled gear of a visit, shared by the party (first buyer): `weapons` weapons and foci and `items` items in the depth's price band (rewards.price_band, on the standard price), and `rare` pieces in the band times `rare_band` at `rare_rarity`; rarity by `rarity` (the last row whose `from_stage` the stage reaches), every roll capped by the stage's ceiling (rewards.ceiling); `item_categories`: the items.json categories it may roll (mods and armour are the Forge's). `restock_price`: credits a point of a persistent class resource. `max_qty`: the most of one counter line in one purchase.

sell_rate.about: Rules 1.42 (spec rule 27, Leon 13 Nov): a sale pays `rate` of the price at the item's own rarity, its fitted mods at theirs (credits.ts priceOf); plot items and the unpriced cannot be sold.

faces.about: Rules 1.42 (spec section 3.4): the faces of the safe nodes: one shopkeeper per setting, one armourer, drill sergeant and medic for every setting, the shrine's patron. `portrait` and `backdrop` are the art/catalog.json ids the artist will deliver (`*_pending: true` until they land); `fallback` is a world-pool portrait (catalog `characters`; the patron's is the rolled patron's own, `fallback_patron`) and `backdrop_fallback` an illustration id (catalog `illustrations`), or null for the ground colour, drawn meanwhile. `bias` weights the rolled stock by tag (weapon, item, melee, thrown, focus, mana, core, mod); `price` multiplies the rolled stock's prices only. `lines`: greet, bought, cant_afford, sold, sold_to (a rolled piece another player took), gave, leave, and what the keeper says as a tab opens (stock, gear, upgrade, sell at a shop; upgrade, stock, fit at a Forge; train, shrine, trade; give), in the keeper's own voice (docs/design/ui-screens.md, Writing for the player); the shrine's patron face has `votaries`: each patron's votary's greet, bought and leave.

greet: Sign for it or don't touch it.
Chapter stores. Everything here is counted twice and blessed once.
You look like someone who just spent a magazine on a wall. Restock.
bought: Signed out to you. Bring back the casing if you can.
That is on the ledger now.
cant_afford: Come back with the credits. The rifle will wait.
sold: I'll find a use for it.
Back into stores. Somebody will be glad of it.
sold_to: Gone. Signed out to someone faster.
gave: Sharing kit. Put it in the ledger.
leave: Bring it back in one piece.
stock: Rounds I always have. The good stuff, you take what's on the table.
Ammunition is the one thing the chapter never runs out of. Allegedly.
gear: Today's issue. One of each, and when it's signed out, it's gone.
First hand on it signs for it.
upgrade: I can clear a jam and file a grade up. Both cost.
Hand it over. I'll make it worth the paperwork.
sell: Back into stores it goes. Don't expect chapter generosity.
I'll take it. The ledger decides what it's worth.
give: Passing kit to a squadmate? Fine. I'm writing it down.

greet: You didn't see me. I didn't see you. Now, what do you need?
Everything here fell off something. The prices are honest, which is more than the streets are.
Keep your voice down and your purse open.
bought: Don't tell anyone where you got it.
cant_afford: Short. I don't do favours, I do business.
stock: Rounds? Always. Nobody asks where rounds come from.
Bullets are the one honest thing I sell.
gear: One of each. Once they walk, they don't come back.
Fresh off a truck that didn't stop.
upgrade: Bent? Busted? I can make it look like it isn't.
I know a man with a file and no questions.
sell: I'll buy it. I won't pay much. That's business.
give: Share with your friends, sure. Less for me to sell them.

greet: Mind the mud. Blades on the left, bangs on the right.
The front takes everything eventually. Take what you need first.
Wipe your boots. Then buy something.
bought: Good choice. Sharp end away from you.
That'll see you through the next trench.
cant_afford: The war doesn't give discounts and neither do I.
sold: I'll sell it to the next poor sod.
gave: Look after each other out there.
leave: Keep your head below the line.
stock: Rounds, shells, grenades. The front always wants more.
Ammo's never short here. Everything else is.
gear: That's what came back from the line today. Take it before someone else does.
One of each. The dead weren't greedy.
upgrade: Mud in the action? Give it here.
I'll make it fit for the front. For a price.
sell: Salvage pays. Not much, but it pays.
give: Pass it along. Somebody'll need it more by tonight.

greet: Smetanita goods. Precision costs, and precision is all I sell.
Gloves, cores, tools of the trade. The foundry makes, I deliver.
Inspect anything. Touch nothing you won't buy.
cant_afford: Quality has a price. You are below it.
stock: Standard consumables, always in stock. The foundry sees to it.
Cores and rounds by the crate. Never a shortage.
gear: Today's consignment. Limited, as precision always is.
Each piece is unique. So is its price.
upgrade: Bring it up to standard. Then above it.
sell: I'll assess it. Expect a fair, small number.

greet: Peace on your road. The relics are blessed; the rounds are merely counted.
Lay down your burdens. Then pick up new ones; they are for sale.
Be welcome, pilgrim. Mind the step, it is older than you.
cant_afford: Faith is free. This is not.
sold: It will find a better owner.
gave: A gift freely given is twice blessed.
leave: Walk in the light, or at least near it.
stock: Rounds and cores, counted and blessed. There are always more.
The house never runs dry of the ordinary things.
gear: Each relic here waits for one owner. Choose.
One of each, as the saints intended.
upgrade: Bring it to the altar. We mend what can be mended.
A blessing on the steel, and a better grade under it.
sell: The house takes it back, and gives a little.
give: Give freely. It is the only giving that counts.

greet: Air's recycled, prices aren't. Take a look.
Last stop before the dark. Stock up.
Close the hatch behind you. We pay for the heat.
cant_afford: Out here nothing's free. Not even breathing.
sold: Everything gets used twice on the rim.
stock: Rounds and cells, always. Out here you don't run dry twice.
Ammunition's the one thing the ships never forget.
gear: Whatever the last ship dropped. One of each.
Take it now. The next ship might not come.
upgrade: Patch it, seal it, grade it. All for a price.
sell: Scrap's worth something on the rim. Not a lot.
give: Share the load. That's how crews get home.

greet: Put it on the bench. Let's see what it could be.
Steel remembers how it was treated. Let's fix that.
Bring me something worth the work.
stock: Mods and plates, cut for what your squad carries.
Made this morning. Made for you lot.
upgrade: One piece on my bench each. Pick the one that matters.
Hand it over. You'll want it back better.
fit: Stand still. I'll fit the next plate to you.
Heavier armour, if your body can take it.

greet: On the line. Again. Until it's boring.
You call that a stance? We'll fix it.
First drill's on me. The second one you pay for.
cant_afford: Extra drill costs. Pay or run laps.
train: Pick your drill. I'll make you hate it.
Once on me, again on your coin.

greet: Sit. Breathe. Let me look at that.
Everyone's patched. Rest while you can.
Nobody leaves until I've seen them.
train: If you've energy left, practise something quiet.

greet: The candles lean toward you.
The shrine is quiet. It is listening.
Someone keeps these candles lit. Not you.
shrine: Take one thing. The shrine gives once.

greet: Kneel if you mean it. Stand if you don't. The saints see both.
Confession is free. Everything after it, you earn.
Mind the candles, child. They have burned longer than you.
bought: Go, with their eye on you.

greet: Name, rank, requisition. In that order.
Every blessing here is counted. Sign where I point.
The war is still on. Take what you're issued.
leave: Report back in one piece. Paperwork otherwise.

greet: Oh, a pilgrim! Pick something. Everything here is real, probably.
Pray if you like. He'll laugh either way.
Take a blessing. Take two. No, one. That was the joke.
leave: Don't trust the next shrine. Or this one.

greet: Every crossing has its toll. This one is paid in faith.
Sit a moment. The water waits for no one, but I do.
The coin box is for the dead. You are not dead yet.
Come in, sit down, you're letting the warm out.
Kettle's on. Have you eaten? You haven't. Sit.
Look at the state of you. Let's see what we can do.
leave: Come back before you're starving this time.

greet: BEHOLD THE SHRINE OF THE STORM. Wipe your feet.
The sky has opinions about you. Mostly good.
Speak up. He can't hear you over himself.
leave: Go. Make a noise about it.

greet: Are you on the list? Everyone's on the list. Sit.
Oh, you'd look lovely together. You and a blessing, I mean.
She has a plan for you. It has a seating chart.
bought: I'll put that in the file.

greet: Your thread is on the loom. Let's see the figures.
Everything is counted here. Including you, twice.
Sit. The Weaver is reconciling your accounts.
leave: Your thread runs on. For now.

greet: Everyone who walks this road wants something. So do I.
Three deals on the table. Pick one, or keep walking.
No haggling. The price is the price.
cant_afford: Come back when you can pay.
leave: The road forks again further on.
trade: One deal each. I'm not running a charity.
Read the terms. I always do.

give.about: Rules 1.46 (spec rule 47; primitive 13): where a character of a run may give another credits or a pack entry: the node kinds with no fight (`where`), and before the first node (`at_start`). A give is plain (no confirm from the receiver) and logged in words. Never given: boons, tokens and the graft (c.relics), trainings, the fitted armour class; a Relic whose property would take the receiver past the boon cap is refused. Out of a run (a campaign) a give is made out of a fight.

map.about: Rules 1.48 (Leon, 13 Nov: lanes; survival-spec rules 7 to 9, section 3.1): the path map. From the start every lane can be chosen; a lane is a run of nodes with exactly one way forward; lanes meet only at junctions (two or three neighbouring lanes, `junction.sizes`, merge into one node and split again), at the gate (every lane), at the final junction (every lane, before row 14's shop and rest) and at the Boss. A segment, a lane's run between two meeting nodes, is `junction.segment` nodes long and takes a theme (`themes`: what it holds, placed where the rules allow; `fill`: what fills the rest, none: fights) distinct from its siblings', so a party picks a lane by reading ahead. `junction_kinds`: what a junction node rolls. `every_route`: kinds every route passes in depths 1 to final_row; `guarantees`: the reference route's windows; `shop_gap`: a shop within that many nodes of the start and of every junction on some route (and the reference route's shops never further apart). One vault a map: a spur of a guard fight and a chest off an edge lane node (`vault.edge`) in `vault.depths`.
